title: Quarterly narrative anchors for exec sync
content:
Purpose / usage: quick scratchpad for framing the leadership/exec staff sync. Not a final deck — this is my working narrative to guide what I say and to capture follow-ups.

Meeting context: weekly exec staff on Thu 9:00am PT. Main asks this week: 1) align on Q2 capacity and Dedicated sales ramp assumptions, 2) decision on conservative traffic routing policy for EMEA outage scenario, 3) surface any new regression risks from the latest model-quantization experiment.

Top-line narrative anchors (what I want execs to take away):
- We are in a healthy place for hosted growth but capacity and cost controls need tightening to avoid surprise egress/spot spikes in May-June.
- Proposed mitigation: temporary conservative routing + two short-lived Dedicated pools for key enterprise customers; small revenue tradeoff for lower risk.
- Model quantization A/B shows ~1.8% latency improvement avg, but there are rare failure modes on 16k-context models that need hotfix MLP patch before wide rollout.

Agenda (15m total time for my section + Q&A):
1) Quick status (2m): usage, cost delta, key incidents since last week (callout: EU-region 03/04).
2) Decision (5m): approve conservative routing policy + sign-off to spin up 2 dedicated pools (cost vs SLA tradeoffs).
3) Risk spotlight (4m): quantization regression surface and mitigation timeline.
4) Ask list & follow-ups (4m): who owns what next 2 weeks.

Data to surface (short bullets I will read or hold up):
- Hosted API 7d RPS change: +14% (esp. embeddings), token spend up 11% YoY (internal dashboard snapshot).
- Incident: EU control-plane failover 03/04 caused 6% p95 latency bump for 18m, root cause: autoscaler edge case INF-2042 (JIRA).
- Cost sensitivity: spinning two small Dedicated pools (~8 A100 equiv) estimated incremental monthly burn +$72k but removes ~65% of high-priority enterprise traffic from hosted central pool.

Hypotheses / recommended decisions:
- H1: Conservative routing (prefer Dedicated/region-first for flagged enterprise customers) will keep SLAs intact and reduce incident blast radius. Recommend 2-week trial windows per customer.
- H2: Quantization can be rolled to 60% of traffic after MLP hotfix and enhanced evals; until then keep Canary at 5% with autoswitch to FP baseline on quality regression.

Short script snippets (spoken cues):
- "Quick reality: we can grow ARR and still be reliable, but it requires preemptive capacity nudges. I'm asking for a small, timeboxed spend to secure enterprise lanes while we tighten routing policies."
- "On quantization — the perf gains are real, but we found edge-case hallucination deltas on long contexts. We have a patch and test plan, but need runway to be conservative with the rollout."

Red/Yellow/Green flags (one-liners to mention):
- RED: Any further unplanned control-plane failover in EU or APAC before May will materially threaten enterprise SLAs for a set of customers (ticket INF-2042).
- YELLOW: Embeddings RPS growth concentrated on a handful of self-serve customers; could cause cost overruns if not throttled with quotas.
- GREEN: Dedicated sales pipeline — 3 near-term deals totaling ~$0.9M ARR; these are the customers we should prioritize for Dedicated pools.

Open questions for execs:
- Approve the temporary conservative routing policy for flagged enterprise accounts? (thumbs up/thumbs down)
- OK to allocate up to +$75k/mo in incremental spend for two small Dedicated pools for a 6–8 week window?
- Any objections to pausing broad quantization until hotfix lands?

Action items (captured during prep, pre-assigned where I think appropriate):
- Priya: draft routing policy language and rollout checklist — due 2026-03-13 EOD. (me)
- Evan McCarthy: authorize procurement path & budget signal for two Dedicated pools; confirm funding source — due 2026-03-14 morning.
- Sofia Ramos: run targeted evals on long-context prompts with patched MLP by 2026-03-16 and report P0 regressions.
- Eng infra (cc: Ben Cho): prioritize INF-2042 fix and provide status update by Thu sync — if not complete, recommend emergency mitigation (route EU control-plane traffic to fallback region).
- Product (cc: Lina Park): identify up to 3 enterprise customers to shift to trial Dedicated pools and confirm contact + comms plan by 2026-03-13.

Parking lot / items to materialize after the sync:
- Draft customer-facing note for affected enterprise customers explaining temporary Dedicated trials and service benefits (ownership: CS).
- Scripted rollback playbook for quantization rollouts with automatic metric-based triggers.
- Short one-pager cost/benefit to present to finance for contingency budget authorization.

Notes to self (quick reminders while presenting):
- Keep language simple: focus on risk reduction and SLA stability, not low-level infra detail.
- Have numbers ready if asked: delta cost, p95 impact, expected lead time to spin pools.
- If asked about timeline: be explicit — 48–72 hours to spin pools once procurement greenlit.

Snippets to paste into follow-up Slack after meeting:
- "Thanks all — agreed to trial conservative routing for flagged enterprise accounts. Action owners: Priya (policy), Evan (budget), Sofia (evals), Ben (INF-2042 fix). I'll post the routing checklist and comms draft by EOD."

Draft remarks (closing, 45–60s):
- "We can keep moving at the current growth velocity, but we need to be surgical about where traffic lands and how we roll model changes. The small, temporary spend here is insurance — it protects our enterprise revenue and buys time to make routing/batching improvements that will lower unit costs long term."

Misc/links I might paste into the slide handout quickly:
- Confluence: Q1 postmortem highlights (link above)
- JIRA: INF-2042 for autoscaler edge-case
- PR: serving-runtime #987 for the quantization rollout guardrails

Version history / notes:
- 2026-03-10 initial draft
- 2026-03-12 updated after chat with Sofia and Evan — added cost numbers and tightened asks

End of scratchpad.
